title: Calendar Meeting Load and Deep-Work Time
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports.
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, and calendar feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:event
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(duration_min) as meeting_min, count as meetings by _time
| eval meeting_h=round(meeting_min/60,1), deep_work_h=round((8-meeting_h),1)
| sort - _time
description: Adds up how many hours of your day meetings consume and what is left for focused work, revealing the days with no room to think.
value: Meeting overload is the enemy of deep work; quantifying the split makes the case to protect focus blocks on your calendar.
implementation: Export calendar events to HEC; schedule daily and review meeting load versus available focus time.
visualization: Stacked column chart of daily meeting hours versus deep-work hours.
grandmaExplanation: It adds up how much of your day is meetings versus time to actually get work done, exposing the overloaded days.
